findings: ColorDescIndex::find explicitly ignores SearchParams and scans every descriptor. It returns all nonzero-ID entries with distance<FLT_MAX, converts float distance to int score, and leaves downstream maxMatches/filtering to Database. This is nearest-color ranking, not an explicit color similarity acceptance threshold.

Float-to-int conversion discards fractional score distinctions before database sorting. No descriptor distance implementation or real-color ordering benchmark reviewed yet, so no quantified ranking impact.

If target.numColors<=0, find tries stored index data by ID, then returns empty if still absent. Grayscale/empty descriptors may be stored and represented by mediaIds yet remain unsearchable through this algorithm. Actual distance behavior for empty candidates still unread.

load preallocates rowCount descriptors/IDs and guards against more rows, but retains _count if fewer rows arrive. A concurrently shrinking table could leave uninitialized allocated tail; static source observation only, no malformed-memory or concurrency test run.

SQL addRecords filters TypeImage while in-memory add appends every Media supplied without a type check. Caller Database add can supply multiple types; actual nonimage ColorDescriptor initialization and resulting runtime behavior need further review.

isLoaded is _count>0, so an empty loaded SQL table remains logically unloaded. A nonempty tombstone-only allocation remains loaded after removals because count is unchanged. Count/memory reflect allocated entries rather than live searchable media.
SQL blobs require exact sizeof(ColorDescriptor), otherwise descriptor.clear is used. Native struct layout is persisted directly, no per-row schema/version portability proof at this layer.

Color-index tests use generic40x5-sizes and assert descriptor+ID memory formula; they do not establish a color-only acceptance threshold, grayscale recall, float-score ordering or concurrent load correctness. No upstream tests executed.
